subtopics.title: The Metric Ladder and the Marks in Units

questions.question: A household is billed for 24 kℓ of water in a month. In litres that is:
The direction rule for metric conversions says:
options: Converting to a SMALLER unit means more of them, so multiply; to a LARGER unit, divide
Multiply for length, divide for mass

questions.question: A room is given as 3,8 m by 260 cm. The correct first move is to:
options: Convert both into the same unit — 3,8 m by 2,6 m — before calculating

questions.question: An answer claiming a kettle holds 4 000 litres should prompt you to:
options: Write it down and move on
Recheck the working — the estimate is far too large for the real world

subtopics.title: Crossing Into Imperial: Inches, Pounds and Miles

questions.question: A 25 kg bag of maize meal, using 1 kg ≈ 2,2 pounds, weighs about:
A woman five foot ten — 70 inches — using 1 inch = 2,54 cm, stands:
A road sign of 45 miles per hour, using 1 mile ≈ 1,609 km, is about:
The dependable way to choose multiply or divide when crossing systems is:
options: Follow the order the units appear in the question
Ask which unit is BIGGER — the bigger unit converts into a larger NUMBER of the smaller one

questions.question: Converting 400 °F to Celsius gives:
options: 204,44 °C, so the oven is set to 200 °C

questions.question: A child's temperature of 39 °C in Fahrenheit is:
The duration from 13:35 to 15:10 is:
A bus leaves Polokwane at 06:50 and travels for five hours twenty-five. It arrives at:

subtopics.title: Proportional Conversions: Coverage, Doses and Recipes

questions.question: Paint covering 30 m² per 5 ℓ is needed for a 51 m² wall given two coats. The volume required is:
With 5 ℓ tins at R465 and a 20 ℓ drum at R1 680, the cheaper way to reach 20 ℓ is:
options: One 20 ℓ drum at R1 680 — R180 cheaper than four tins
Both routes cost exactly the same

questions.question: A dose of 10 mℓ twice a day for seven days needs:
options: 140 mℓ — so two 120 mℓ bottles must be bought

questions.question: Scaling a recipe for 6 up to 27 servings, the 3 eggs become:
options: 13,5 eggs, so 14 eggs are bought — quantities like eggs and paint round UP

questions.question: The number the entire metric system is built on is:
options: One thousand — millimetres in a metre, metres in a kilometre, grams in a kilogram, millilitres in a litre

questions.question: The unit that breaks the thousand rhythm is:
options: The centimetre — there are a hundred in a metre

questions.question: Which everyday anchor is useful for estimating?
options: A brick is about a metre long
A teaspoon holds about a litre
A walking stride is roughly a metre and a big cool drink bottle holds two litres
A bag of mealie meal weighs about a tonne

questions.question: When one measurement is in centimetres and another in metres, you should:
options: Convert both into the same unit FIRST, then calculate

questions.question: Coming DOWN from Fahrenheit to Celsius, the order of steps is:
options: Subtract 32 first, then multiply by 5, then divide by 9
Multiply by 9, divide by 5, then subtract 32

questions.question: Temperature needs a formula rather than a single multiplier because:
options: The scales do not start at the same place — water freezes at 0 °C but at 32 °F
Celsius is metric and metric always uses 1 000

questions.question: An imported bag labelled 44 pounds, at 2,2 pounds per kilogram, is:

subtopics.title: How Much Paint, How Much Medicine

questions.question: If 5 ℓ of paint covers 30 m², one litre covers:
A complete answer to "what should the painter buy?" is:
options: One 20 ℓ drum at R1 680 — R180 cheaper than four 5 ℓ tins at R1 860
Four tins, because tins are easier to carry

questions.question: Scaling a recipe from 6 servings to 27 means multiplying every quantity by:
The rounding rule that fits the context is:
options: Round everything to the nearest whole number
Round everything down to be safe
Round only at the start of the calculation
Round paint and eggs UP, round money to cents, and never round a medicine dose
